variant_reviews.comparison: Keep P0 fixed; for each P1 in P take an infimum jointly over the estimator and Q in the channel class of the maximum of the two risks at P0,P1, then take the outer supremum over P1. This permits the chosen procedure to depend on the two-point problem and is not inf-over-procedures followed by sup-over-all-P. The observed law Q composed with P is the marginal private sequence generated from iid raw X_i and history-dependent Q kernels, not automatically a product of one-observation output laws. avgRisk at a Dirac prior can express one fixed-P risk after constructing that experiment, but a prior average is not the displayed maximum. Nonnegative extended integrals avoid treating infinite loss expectations as the Bochner integral's default zero; empty estimator/channel classes and finite-real extrema need their own conventions.
